questions.question: How should the six runs get sysmon? (Applies only if the re-measure, running now, shows identical coverage.) Hatch scripts have no per-command env syntax, and an `env COVERAGE_CORE=sysmon …` prefix would break `hatch run all` for Windows contributors.

options.label: coverage config (Recommended)
options.description: `[tool.coverage.run] core = "sysmon"` + `disable_warnings = ["no-sysmon"]` in pyproject. One line, cross-platform, reaches all six with no ci.yml edit. Coverage falls back to the default core by itself on 3.11 and for --cov-branch on 3.12/3.13, so test-cov-branch's effective core stays the same (to be verified per interpreter). Also reaches ad-hoc `pytest --cov` runs. Hides the fallback warning.

options.label: ci.yml env + hatch env-vars
options.description: `COVERAGE_CORE: sysmon` as job-level env on the three ci.yml jobs (explicit), plus `[tool.hatch.envs.default.env-vars]` for local. The hatch part applies to the whole default env, test-cov-branch included, and its no-sysmon fallback warning may trip filterwarnings=error unless also disabled.

options.label: ci.yml env only, POSIX prefix
options.description: Job-level env in ci.yml plus `env COVERAGE_CORE=sysmon` prefixes on the three hatch scripts. Most literal match to the item's six, but breaks those scripts (and `hatch run all`) on Windows cmd/PowerShell.
